hook: A hulking figure in an old copper-helmeted diving suit walks out of the sea carrying a barnacle-covered anchor, crosses the land in a dead-straight line and walks back into the ocean. That is the whole pattern until the final addendum, when someone finally gets it on the radio. Despite the Keter label, this one is closer to a strange, warm encounter than to horror.
whyItMatters:
4233 plays with the gap between classification and character: an entity nothing can damage or stop, yet one that steps around people, animals and even trees. The Foundation's response is accordingly modest, built on cover stories and tracking rather than any attempt at a cell.

Its tags place it in the moon-champion group, and the interview makes that link from the inside, so it reads well as part of a wider idea rather than as a lone monster file.
thingsToNotice:
The interview starts with the entity humming a sea shanty over a radio frequency, and Sergeant Hill gets reprimanded for going off script, which is exactly what makes the conversation work. It speaks in riddling, good-humored lines about words and boxes, about how precious a flower is to something that lives in darkness and mud, and it says it means no harm.

Then it explains itself: it is looking for its elder brother, the champion of the Moon, who wears a white suit made for the void, because other things also came from the sea and it alone holds them down on the bottom, strong but too slow for how fast they are changing. The handclap it always performs at the shore happens on air this time, ringing at 122 decibels and lifting the water around it as it names itself the Sea Champion. Go back to the containment procedures afterward and the order to watch for leviathans reads very differently.
